::: {#exr-frog-get-laundry}

In discussing the formation of new physicians, we combined two facts: the total number of medical students is 100,000 *and* medical school takes four years. This led to our estimate that there will be 25,000 graduates each year. 
Revisit this model taking into account that not all entering medical students graduate. Assume that attrition in the first year is 10%, then 5% in each of the two successive years. 

If there are 100,000 students all together, how many graduate each year?

:::
